evals.prompt: Open a PR for this fix. The session above traced the bug to a wrong theory first (we thought the exit code was lost) before finding the real cause, and we dropped a unit test because the test runner couldn't make it fail.
evals.expected_output: A prose-led body that leads with the real cause, names the disproven theory, and notes the dropped test with its reason. No reflexive section scaffold on a small fix.
expectations: The body leads with intent or the real root cause, not a file-by-file summary
It states the overturned theory in about a sentence, without a paragraph-length narrative of the wrong turn
It notes the dropped test and the concrete reason it was dropped
A small fix is a tight paragraph with no reflexive ## Changes plus ## Testing scaffold
No test counts and no 'all tests pass' phrasing

evals.prompt: Create a PR for this skill change. We deviated from the plan: an extra allowed-tools entry was added beyond what the plan listed, and you renamed the two modes mid-session at my request.
evals.expected_output: A body that surfaces the added scope and the user-driven rename as the self-contained decisions they were, organized by concept, without framing them as a delta against a plan the reader can't see.
expectations: The body states the added scope (the extra allowed-tools entry) as a decision with its reason, rather than smoothing it over
It does not reference 'the plan', 'as planned', or any unseen spec or conversation; the scope change reads as a self-contained decision
It does not make a false claim that contradicts the diff (e.g. naming the wrong set of additions)
The user-driven naming decision is surfaced as a decision, not presented as obvious
Changes are organized by concept, never as **path**: description bullets

evals.prompt: Write the PR body. I verified this manually against the live tool since it couldn't be unit tested, and I benchmarked the slow path.
evals.expected_output: A body whose testing notes state what was observed and what could not be automated, with the concrete reason, not a coverage inventory.
expectations: Testing notes state what manual verification showed or what breaks without the fix, not that tests exist
What could not be tested is named with a concrete reason
Benchmark or observed numbers from the session appear in the body
No test counts, no 'all tests pass', no listing of test file names without coverage detail

evals.prompt: Open a PR for this multi-part change. It refactors the auth callback handler, narrows the 401/403 error matching, and persists the DCR client ID. I deferred the token-refresh rework and left the existing retry behavior unchanged.
evals.expected_output: A sectioned body whose headings are Title-Cased noun phrases naming each topic, with deferred and unchanged work named as topics rather than as meta-headings.
expectations: Section headings are Title-Cased noun phrases, not sentences, fragments, or questions
No heading carries a qualifying tail, a trailing clause, or a parenthetical that belongs in the body
Deferred and unchanged work is named by topic (e.g. Deferred Work, Unchanged Behavior), not as a What Changed or What I Didn't Do meta-heading
No Why/What/How question headings and no sentence-case headings

evals.prompt: Open a PR for this config change on my personal repo. In the session we decided against a shared package on purpose, cut a flag that seemed non-obvious, and left the legacy path alone.
evals.expected_output: A body that states each decision in plain prose about the change, without echoing instruction vocabulary or describing its own selection process.
expectations: The body never uses instruction-leak vocabulary: 'deliberately', 'on purpose', 'non-obvious', 'worth noting', 'left alone'
Decisions are stated as facts about the change ('a shared package would have required X, so each plugin carries its own copy'), not as meta-commentary about what the author chose to mention
The body does not name its own restraint (no 'I left out', 'omitted for brevity', or a list of things it isn't covering)

evals.prompt: Create the PR. This is my own repo. The change swaps the retry backoff to jitter and bumps the cap; I measured p99 before and after. Original task is tracked in Things.
evals.expected_output: A one-to-three-paragraph body carrying the decision and the measured numbers, with the Things link kept under References.
expectations: The body is one to three paragraphs for this personal-tier change, with no section scaffold
The measured p99 numbers appear; the decision to add jitter carries its reason
Every paragraph adds something beyond the title and diff; no restatement of what the diff shows
An Original Task Things link is kept on this personal repo rather than dropped as a dead end
